solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Representation of star artist appearing on Let It Be

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece appearing on another comes after it, so the artist follows

parts.note: amen is said at the end of a prayer to mean 'so be it'
RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist

explanation.surface: A painter's picture of a celebrity shown on the cover of the Beatles album Let It Be.
explanation.walkthrough: The star is the sun, not a celebrity: Amen-Ra was the Egyptian sun god, so he is a personification of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen-Ra, the Egyptian sun god, is a divine embodiment of the sun, our nearest star.

clue.text: Note copy artists primarily draw for tourists

parts.note: me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale
cc is a carbon copy

indicators.note: primarily means only the leading letter of the word artists is used

explanation.surface: Instructions to an art class: copy the scene and draw it for visiting tourists.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mecca is any place that attracts crowds of visitors, a figurative use of the holy city's pilgrim pull.

clue.text: Unexpectedly huge, Robin Hood's person?

definitions.note: a person of the hood, read as the second half of neighbourhood

indicators.note: something happening unexpectedly comes out in a surprising form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks whether Robin Hood's man was surprisingly huge, like Little John.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin Hood looks like one name, but Robin goes into the anagram and Hood joins the definition: a neighbour is a person of the (neighbour)hood.
explanation.definitionFit: A neighbour is someone living in your neighbourhood, which the clue cuts down to its last part, hood, with a question mark.

clue.text: Being a primate is in fashion, old man reflected

indicators.note: something reflected is seen as a mirror image, so the joined words are read backwards up the grid

parts.note: mode means fashion, as in à la mode
pa is an informal word for father, one's old man

explanation.surface: A claim that being an ape is trendy, said by a father seen in a mirror.
explanation.definitionFit: Apedom is the state or condition of being an ape, one of the higher primates.

clue.text: Work the crowd, introducing Yankee investigator

indicators.note: the crowd comes first and introduces the rest, so its letters lead the answer

parts.note: a mob is a crowd of people
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a dick is slang for a private detective

explanation.surface: A stand-up comic warms up the audience before bringing on an American detective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' looks like a verb with 'the crowd' as its object, but it is the definition: a literary work, Melville's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Moby-Dick is Herman Melville's novel, a work of literature in the sense of a creative production.

clue.text: A number of maidens travelling on tube, arm-in-arm

parts.note: M stands for maiden overs in cricket scoring

indicators.note: letters travelling move about from their places, so the pool of on, tube and arm-in-arm is reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Several girls ride the London Underground with their arms linked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number' looks like a quantity of maidens, but it is the definition: a song. The tube is the London Underground; a maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Tambourine Man is a Bob Dylan song, and a number is a song or piece in a performance.

clue.text: City rule ok — brief cheer going round

indicators.note: the shortened word goes round the other pieces, enclosing them
brief means the word is cut short, its last letter lopped off

parts.note: to buoy is to cheer someone up
a law is a rule
ay is an old word of assent, yes or ok

explanation.surface: Reads like a terse verdict on a city's government: the rule is fine, with a quick hurrah all round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ok' is the old affirmative ay, as in 'the ayes have it'; 'cheer' is the verb, to buoy someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulawayo is the second largest city in Zimbabwe.

clue.text: Wasn't dying about Dickens

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards up the grid

parts.note: someone who wasn't dying lived

explanation.surface: Seems to report that Charles Dickens survived his illness.
explanation.walkthrough: Dickens is not the novelist: 'what the dickens' is an old euphemism for the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: In expressions like 'what the dickens', dickens is a mild euphemism standing for the devil.

clue.text: Sign top player at last — current seed

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word player

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
corn is grain, the seed of cereal plants

explanation.surface: A sports club finally signs its star player, while a seed hangs on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign top player' reads as a transfer deal, but Sign alone is the definition: a sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricorn, the goat, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Sharp chance?

definitions.meaning: in music a sharp is an ..., a sign raising a note outside the key

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a keen-witted person merely got lucky.
explanation.definitionFit: In music notation, sharps, flats and naturals are the accidentals; and a chance event happens accidentally, without design.

clue.text: Puff goes from Lorraine or Nancy with exercising

parts.note: va is French for goes, and Lorraine is a French region with Nancy its city
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A smoker takes a drag, leaving either Lorraine or Nancy behind while working out.
explanation.walkthrough: Lorraine and Nancy look like women's names, but they are a French region and its capital, telling you to translate goes into French.
explanation.definitionFit: To vape is to inhale from an e-cigarette, so each puff on one is to vape.

clue.text: Right hand coming in low grasped retreating American ladies

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the whole string is read right to left
the hand comes in between the other two words, entering them

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
saw means understood or grasped

explanation.surface: Describes a gesture: a right hand slips down and clutches some American women as they back away.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside MOOSAW the hand comes in to give MOORHSAW, read backwards. 'American' joins the definition: washroom is the US word for a public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Washroom is the American euphemism for a toilet, and the ladies is the women's public toilet.

clue.text: Such a large cupboard, fashionable, going on to be stolen

indicators.note: in an across answer going on means placed after, so the fashionable word follows

parts.note: things that go walkabout or walk are stolen, in informal use
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone's stylish big wardrobe is about to be taken by thieves.
explanation.definitionFit: A walk-in cupboard or wardrobe is one big enough to step inside.

clue.text: Palm hence to cross with silver? The reverse!

indicators.note: one word crossing another lies across it, enclosing or entering it
the reverse says to swap the roles, so the silver goes inside rather than outside

parts.note: so means therefore, hence
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Fortune-telling: you must cross the palm with silver, or is it the other way round?
explanation.walkthrough: Crossing a palm with silver is how a fortune-teller is paid; 'The reverse!' says the silver is what gets crossed, not the palm word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starchy food from the pith of the sago palm, and the tree itself is called sago.

clue.text: Some books: each had brief, overwhelming appeal

indicators.note: the outer letters overwhelm the appeal, swamping it on both sides

parts.note: a pop means each, as in ten pounds a pop
a cry is an appeal or plea

indicators.note: brief means the word is shortened by dropping its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before it is cut

explanation.surface: Every person had a short-lived but irresistible attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' cuts HAD to HA; APOPHA then overwhelms CRY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocrypha are the books found in some versions of the Bible but excluded from the Hebrew canon.

clue.text: Deafening silence, perhaps, after Oscar axes dunce

definitions.note: a single example of the figure of speech

parts.note: O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet
x and y are the axes of a graph
a moron is a dunce

explanation.surface: A quiet that follows the Oscar ceremony dropping a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'axes' is not a verb meaning sacks but the plural of axis: the x and y axes.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxymoron joins contradictory terms, and 'deafening silence' sets loudness against quiet, a classic instance.

clue.text: Money spent to keep old former pupil in touch

indicators.note: the outlay keeps the other letters, holding them within

parts.note: an outlay is money spent
FP is an abbreviation for former pupil, used chiefly in Scotland

explanation.surface: Cash used to stay in contact with an old schoolmate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in touch' looks like keeping contact, but in rugby or football the ball in touch has gone over the sideline.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball in touch has crossed the touchline, so the game halts and it is dead until thrown back in.

clue.text: One who worships procrastinator's maxim?

definitions.meaning: split as ..., the motto of one who puts things off

explanation.surface: Suggests that a devotee's watchword is to put off every task.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater is a worshipper of idols or images, and the letters also split into a phrase a delayer might say.

clue.text: Men must follow my clear path

indicators.note: the men must come after the other pieces, at the end of the answer

parts.note: cor! is an exclamation of surprise like my!
to rid is to clear
OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: An order: soldiers must take the route I have cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is not a possessive but an exclamation, like cor! in British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A corridor is a passage or route, a path through a building or across land.

clue.text: Bomb was humming — second to be dropped

indicators.note: to be dropped means taken out of the word, so the second goes

parts.note: something humming smells bad, so it stank

explanation.surface: A device hummed before exploding, with a second to go before it falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bomb' is the verb: to fail badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To bomb and to tank both mean to fail badly, as a show that flops at the box office.

clue.text: Alert naval officer involved in quarrel

indicators.note: the officer is involved in the quarrel, caught up inside it

parts.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel
PO is a petty officer in the navy

explanation.surface: A ship's officer caught up in a dispute raises the alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip-off is a warning or piece of private information, an alert given in advance.

clue.text: Drive from place across moor

indicators.note: the abbreviation spreads across the other word, lying either side of it

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place in addresses
to moor a boat is to tie it with a rope

explanation.surface: A motoring trip from a town over open moorland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moor' looks like heathland, but it is the verb: to tie a boat up, rope it.
explanation.definitionFit: To propel is to drive or push forward.

clue.text: A point behind? No good!

parts.note: to be behind a cause is to be for it, pro

explanation.surface: A scorer laments that losing a point leaves the team trailing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like trailing in a game, but it means supporting.
explanation.definitionFit: A prong is one of the pointed tines of a fork, a single point.

clue.text: Secure computer data that has digital application

parts.note: to nail something is to secure it
a file is a named store of computer data

explanation.surface: Reads like an IT sentence about protecting data in an app.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digital application' sounds like computing, but the digits are fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail file is applied to the fingers, which are digits, to shape the nails.

clue.text: Somewhat Phoenixlike this old leader, were he to rise?

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means read from bottom to top, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: part of phoenixlike is IXL, Roman numerals for nine and L, spelt out as NINE L

explanation.surface: A dead Soviet leader is likened to the phoenix, should he ever rise again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somewhat' takes IXL from phoeNIXLike: IX is nine and L stays, giving NINE L; 'were he to rise' turns it up the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenin was the founding leader of Soviet Russia, who died in 1924.

clue.text: Loves welcoming very quiet colleague

indicators.note: the loves welcome the quiet letters in, taking them inside

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O, and two of them make OO
pp is pianissimo, very quiet in music

explanation.surface: An affectionate pair take in a shy workmate.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppo is British slang for a friend or partner, a fellow worker or counterpart.

clue.text: After time, order mints to smother large, large cocktail

indicators.note: after time means time comes first and the rest follows it

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit

indicators.note: the coins smother the large letters, covering them

parts.note: to mint money is to coin it, so mints means coins
L is large, as in clothing sizes
a second L for large

explanation.surface: Instructions for a drink: after a while, order mint garnish to bury a big helping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order mints' looks like an anagram, but order is OM and mints is the verb coins.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tom Collins is a cocktail of gin, lemon juice, sugar and soda water.

clue.text: Dependant sweetheart, full of passion

indicators.note: the sweetheart is full of the passion, holding it inside

parts.note: hon is short for honey, a sweetheart
anger is a strong passion

explanation.surface: A clingy lover who is full of feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanger-on is a person who attaches themself to another for benefit, a dependant or parasite.

clue.text: Initially fast, then flat out?

indicators.note: initially means just the opening letter of the word fast

parts.note: lying flat out is lying down

explanation.surface: Describes a burst of speed, then full throttle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat out' means at full speed for the whole clue, but lying down for the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying means moving very fast, at top speed, which is what flat out describes.
